From: Jane Park <jane.park@acme-payments.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden drop in reserved throughput — urgent

Soojin,

We started seeing a sudden increase in 5xx errors and tail latency around 07:45 PT. Our dashboards show sustained token throughput ~40% below our reserved commit for the last 20 minutes, and several inference endpoints falling into queueing. This is hitting user-facing flows for payment fraud scoring.

Can you confirm whether this is a problem on your side (reserved capacity starvation) or if something changed in our traffic? We need a short statement to include in our Ops channel and to escalate internally.

Attached is a small chart and a CSV with sampling windows. We're on a monthly reserved plan (DEAL-4832).

—Jane

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I'm triaging this now and have looped in Ops (David) and my manager (Marissa). Initial checks: our side is reporting a spike in concurrent KV cache misses and elevated batching latency across the dedicated pool servicing your reservation. No automated fallback triggered yet, but there's visible headroom erosion in the pool serving US-East.

Immediate next steps we are initiating now:
- David will open an incident bridge and share the link.
- We'll validate whether a noisy tenant caused temporary eviction from the dedicated pool or whether kernel scheduling changed during the model hot path.
- If confirmed as reserved shortfall, we'll enable a short burst expansion to cover tail latency while we stabilize.

I'll follow up in 15–20 minutes with the incident link and a short customer-ready statement.

—Soojin

Subject: RE: Sudden drop in reserved throughput — urgent

Incident bridge: https://pager.redwood/bridge/INC-72291 (Ops access only)

Quick summary of findings (first 20 min):
- Dedicated pool US-EAST-3 servicing Acme's reservation saw a rapid increase in long-running KV cache misses (correlated with a tenant using long histories + large sequence lengths).
- Autoscaler didn't trigger additional dedicated nodes due to a conservative burst policy being hit (burst budget depleted for that pool).
- Observed a 38% reduction in average reserved throughput across the reservation window; tail gen latency increased from 140ms to 620ms on p95.
- No model bundle changes were pushed from Redwood in the last 24 hours.

Mitigation steps taken (in-progress):
1) Throttled the noisy tenant's queue at the scheduler to free immediate headroom (risk: minor latency bump for that tenant).
2) Manually opened a short-duration burst capacity to add two GPUs to the pool (eta: ~7 minutes).
3) Enabled immediate fallback routing for non-critical routes to a lower-cost model variant to preserve correctness for critical endpoints.

Customer communication suggestion (to send after confirm): \"We're seeing a reserved-capacity headroom shortfall caused by an unexpected spike in long-history inference requests in the shared host pool. We've throttled the offending traffic and opened short burst capacity to restore your throughput; we're monitoring and will confirm when traffic is fully normalized.\"

I'll keep the bridge active until stabilized.

—David
David Kim

Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Production reserved throughput deficit — Acme Payments impact

Thanks everyone for the fast triage. Final status update for the execs and for Acme:

Root cause: a single tenant's batch configuration, coupled with long-history KV cache misses, caused temporary headroom exhaustion in US-EAST-3. The autoscaler respected burst budget limits and did not scale fast enough for the observed access pattern.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: noisy tenant throttled and 2-GPU burst provisioned; throughput restored to >= 98% of reserved commit within 9 minutes.
- Near term (48–72 hours): enlarge burst budget for US-EAST-3 pools by 30%, and add a safeguard that auto-promotes certain priority reservations during headroom erosion.
- Post-mortem: full RCA, telemetry retention around KV miss patterns, and a new autoscaler tuning PR to be deployed next sprint.

Customer remediation offer: approve a pro-rated credit equal to 3 days of reserved fees (we absorbed the immediate burst cost). Sergio/Legal — please draft the credit memo to Acme and confirm entitlement.

Jane — appreciate your partnership on this; we will follow up with a formal RCA and the mitigations plan by EOD Wed. If you want an executive-level brief in the meantime, Marissa and I can join.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
